genericParameters.ownerTokenRule: CLR !n maps to the nth declared owner generic parameter name

errors.propertyAccessorRule: a-getter-and-its-own-setter-are-classified-independently; property|Name marks both and is only correct when the reference IL validates on read and on write

bclInterfaceRelationships.rule: a non-XNA CLR interface an XNA type declares contributes NO projected Go surface of its own
satisfiedBy: the XNA type already declares the interface's members publicly, so the concrete method set is the whole projection
the XNA type implements the interface explicitly, so the CLR member is private .override and is not public surface at all
bclInterfaceRelationships.exhaustive: every non-XNA direct interface in the profile is declared here; an undeclared one is INTERFACE_MAPPING_MISMATCH

declared.System.IDisposable: adds no Disposable interface, no Close alias, no io.Closer adaptation, no finalizer, and no ownership wrapper; 28 of its 29 declaring types declare Dispose publicly and it maps as an ordinary member, while GraphicsDeviceManager implements it explicitly so nothing is projected for it
declared.System.IEquatable`1: the declaring type already declares the strongly typed Equals publicly
declared.System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable`1: projected by the collection rule as GetEnumerator
declared.System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerator`1: projected by the collection rule as Iterator<T> or the collection's own enumerator
declared.System.Collections.Generic.ICollection`1: a concrete Go method set on the XNA collection
declared.System.Collections.Generic.IList`1: its indexer and index methods are already public members of the XNA collection

bclInterfaceRelationships.disposeMembersRemainPerType: a Dispose() or Dispose(bool) the XNA type declares itself stays an ordinary XNA member under the existing overload and per-operation fallibility rules; none is ever synthesized from CLR ancestry
bclInterfaceRelationships.ownershipIsNotSettled: mapping the interface makes a dependency syntactically complete; it does not decide native ownership or lifetime for any concrete type

internalXNAInterfaces.rule: an XNA-namespaced interface that is not a public contract type is assembly-visible, so it contributes no public surface for a stronger reason than a BCL interface: it has no public member to project
internalXNAInterfaces.exhaustive: declared like the BCL set; an XNA interface that is neither a public contract type nor declared internal is INTERFACE_MAPPING_MISMATCH

declared.Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.IGraphi: `.class interface private`; device-loss plumbing declared by seven public graphics types
declared.Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.IDynami: `.class interface private`; content-loss plumbing declared by four public graphics types, whose public ContentLost event is their own declared member

pureManagedClasses.effect: removes-only-the-synthetic-native-runtime-error-result; it never removes an authoritative managed argument failure

collectionInterfaces.System.Collections.Generic.IList<T>: concrete-go-method-set-on-the-xna-collection-no-fake-bcl-package; its indexer and index methods are already declared public members of the XNA collection and map as ordinary members
collectionInterfaces.mutationPolicy: versioned-fail-fast-error-on-next WHERE THE UNDERLYING LIST HAS A VERSION; the policy belongs to the list, not to the view, so an array-backed ReadOnlyCollection<T> is deliberately not version-checked because SZGenericArrayEnumerator<T> has no version to check
collectionInterfaces.concreteEnumeratorRule: a-collection-that-declares-its-own-public-enumerator-type-projects-that-type-from-GetEnumerator; the Iterator<T> adapter is for collections that declare none
collectionInterfaces.inheritedFromAComposedBase: a type that acquires ICollection<T>/IList<T> through a COMPOSED BCL base projects what that base makes PUBLIC, not the full interface: Collection<T> implements ICollection<T>.IsReadOnly explicitly, so it is not public surface and is not projected, and every member the adapter records as excluded is verified ABSENT from the Go type

events.handler: System.EventHandler<T> -> EventHandler[T]; the generic argument is mapped exactly and never degraded to any, a bare func, a channel, or a callback word
events.handlerErrorResult: GO_LANGUAGE_PROJECTION of the CLR exception channel, never an additional XNA return identity
events.eventArgs: System.EventArgs -> *framework.EventArgs; a CLR class keeps reference semantics, so nil is not the projection of EventArgs.Empty and neither any, struct{}, nor map[string]any is admitted
events.eventArgsEmpty: System.EventArgs.Empty -> framework.EventArgsEmpty(), one stable private singleton behind a function so no consumer can reassign the shared identity
events.accessorPair: one CLR event -> exactly two projected Go accessors, unchanged from the settled rule
events.subscriptionIdentity: GO_LANGUAGE_PROJECTION: Go func values are not comparable, so a token names the registration rather than the handler; adding one handler twice yields two registrations and two tokens, unlike CLR Delegate.Remove identity matching
events.nilHandler: Add(nil) registers nothing and returns the zero token, mirroring Delegate.Combine(existing, null) returning existing
events.absentToken: the zero token, an already-removed token, and a token owned by another event all leave every registration list unchanged, mirroring Delegate.Remove of an absent delegate
events.dispatch: registration order over a snapshot taken under the lock; mutation during a raise affects later raises only
events.dispatchFailure: the first non-nil handler error propagates, no later handler runs, and the registration list survives the failure
events.lockScope: no internal lock is held while a consumer handler runs
events.supportTypes: EventSource[T] is public language support so a type declared outside CNA-Go can implement an event-bearing XNA contract; it is measured as an adapter and adds no XNA identity

bclBaseRelationships.rule: a non-XNA CLR base is a measured relationship, never exported Go embedding; Go has no CLR inheritance and embedding would promote members the XNA contract never declared
bclBaseRelationships.derivedProjection: a derived XNA class projects as its own pointer reference type
bclBaseRelationships.addsProjectedSurface: false for IMPLIED, MAPPED and DEFERRED; a COMPOSED base is the one exception and its contribution is counted as BCL_INHERITED_MEMBER_PROJECTIONS, never as an XNA-declared reference member
bclBaseRelationships.exhaustive: every non-XNA base in the profile is declared here; an undeclared base is BASE_MAPPING_MISMATCH, so no base can be dropped in silence
bclBaseRelationships.deferredMeaning: a DEFERRED base is still an open public-API decision, and no derived type may be projected until it is taken
bclBaseRelationships.composedMeaning: a COMPOSED base is a supported BCL family whose PUBLIC members remain part of the observable public CLR surface of every derived type; the derived Go type holds a PRIVATE generic adapter for the base and re-exposes those members through measured forwarding, so the surface does not disappear merely because the XNA assembly metadata does not declare it

deferredDetail.System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary`2: BLOCKED on the public surface mapping, not on the behavior. Six public members of the pinned Dictionary<K,V> cannot be projected in already-decided terms: GetObjectData(SerializationInfo, StreamingContext) and OnDeserialization(object) are PUBLIC, not explicit, and need the System.Runtime.Serialization subsystem; Keys and Values return the public nested KeyCollection/ValueCollection, each with its own surface and nested enumerator; Comparer returns IEqualityComparer<TKey>; and GetEnumerator returns the public nested Dictionary<K,V>.Enumerator over KeyValuePair<K,V>. Projecting a subset would make LaunchParameters a partial type. LaunchParameters is the only consumer.
deferredDetail.System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC: DEFERRED AS A BASE ONLY; it is SUPPORTED as a signature adapter. Its four base consumers -- ModelBoneCollection, ModelEffectCollection, ModelMeshCollection, ModelMeshPartCollection -- are each blocked on their element type (ModelBone, Effect, ModelMesh, ModelMeshPart) and on their own nested Enumerator type, and each also DECLARES a GetEnumerator that HIDES the inherited one, which is an unresolved projection question: CNA-Go projects no base type through which a hidden inherited member could be reached. No consumer needs the answer yet.

expectedCountFormula.provenance: REFERENCE_MEMBERS names only what the Microsoft XNA assemblies declare and is never inflated with inherited mscorlib members; BCL_INHERITED_MEMBER_PROJECTIONS is counted separately and the two partitions are disjoint and exhaustive

languageAdapterPackage: every language adapter is declared in the framework package and takes the same package qualification as any other framework-package name
crossPackageCycleRule: when an ancestor namespace member returns a descendant namespace type that imports ancestor values, project the accessor as a descendant-package function named OwnerTypeMember

bclBaseAdapters.rule: a CLR class that inherits a supported BCL collection base projects as a concrete Go reference type CONTAINING a private generic adapter for that base, which re-exposes the inherited public surface through measured forwarding members
bclBaseAdapters.exportedEmbeddingIsForbidden: type X struct { Collection[T] } is refused: it publishes a Go type the contract never declares, promotes a method set the derived type never declared, implies a Go subtype relationship CLR inheritance does not create, and exposes support implementation; the verifier rejects it
bclBaseAdapters.adapterVisibility: the adapter type and the field that holds it are both unexported, and no projected signature ever names either; when a COMPOSED base gains a consumer outside the framework package the adapter moves to an internal package rather than becoming exported
bclBaseAdapters.hookArchitecture: the base's protected virtual members are projected as an UNEXPORTED Go interface, so only a type declared in this module can supply or reach a hook; every mutating public operation routes through it, so a subclass override always runs and nothing appends to the backing store and separately fakes the override's observable effect
bclBaseAdapters.storageExposure: forbidden: the backing store is never returned, never aliased into a caller's hands, and never an exported field, and a Dictionary-derived or Collection-derived type is never projected as a bare map[K]V or []T
bclBaseAdapters.behaviorAuthority: inherited behavior comes from the exact .NET Framework BCL the pinned XNA assemblies bind against, read from IL, never from modern .NET and never from Go convention; a family whose exact behavior cannot be established stays DEFERRED

System.Collections.ObjectModel.Collectio.authority: mscorlib.dll 4.0.30319.1 (RTMRel.030319-0100), assembly version 4.0.0.0, public key token b77a5c561934e089
System.Collections.ObjectModel.Collectio.backingStore: the parameterless constructor assigns new List<T>(), which is the only overload any pinned XNA subclass calls, so items.IsReadOnly is statically false and the read-only guard on six public mutators is dead for every consumer in the profile

excluded.constructors: the CLR does not inherit constructors; a derived type projects its own
excluded.protectedMembers: Items and the four virtual hooks are `family`; Items would hand out the backing store and the hooks are the private override interface
excluded.explicitInterfaceImplementations: fourteen private .override members of IList, ICollection, IEnumerable and ICollection<T>.IsReadOnly; the settled BCL-interface rule projects nothing for them, so no IsReadOnly, IsSynchronized, SyncRoot or IsFixedSize is invented

System.Collections.ObjectModel.Collectio.enumeration: GetEnumerator returns the backing List<T>'s enumerator boxed as IEnumerator<T>, so enumeration is source order and fail-fast against List<T>._version; the version check runs BEFORE the bounds test, and List<T>.Clear increments the version unconditionally, so clearing an already empty collection still invalidates a live enumerator
System.Collections.ObjectModel.Collectio.enumeratorProjection: the settled Iterator<T> adapter; fusing MoveNext and Current makes the CLR enumerator's default(T) states before the first step and after the last unrepresentable rather than reinvented, and Reset is a private explicit implementation that projects nothing
System.Collections.ObjectModel.Collectio.elementEquality: EqualityComparer<T>.Default, supplied per consumer rather than assumed; for an element type whose CLR form is a reference type that does not override Object.Equals it reduces to reference identity, which Go's == on an interface value spells exactly

bclBaseAdapters.identityAccounting: every projected Go member has exactly one provenance class -- XNA-declared or BCL-inherited -- and every inherited projection is attributable to an exact BCL base, an exact CLR member, and an exact projected Go member

bclSignatureAdapters.rule: a BCL type the pinned XNA contract carries at a PUBLIC SIGNATURE POSITION needs a public Go spelling, or the member that returns it cannot be projected at all; this is the footing System.TimeSpan and System.EventHandler<T> already have
bclSignatureAdapters.distinctFromBaseAdapters: a base adapter is PRIVATE machinery a derived type composes and forwards; a signature adapter is a PUBLIC type because a projected member returns one. One CLR type may hold both roles independently, and neither implies the other
bclSignatureAdapters.surfaceIsMeasured: the adapter's exported member set is pinned to the exact public CLR member inventory, so an adapter type is not a hole in the unexpected-member scan; a missing, extra, or promoted-excluded member is LANGUAGE_MAPPING_MISMATCH

System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC.readOnlyMeaning: no public mutation THROUGH THIS SURFACE, not immutable storage: the type stores the IList<T> it is given rather than copying it, so the owner keeps writing and every change is visible through the view; freezing a copy would be a different type
System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC.readOnlyIsNotANewDecision: every mutator -- ICollection<T>.Add/Clear/Remove, IList<T>.Insert/RemoveAt/set_Item and the whole non-generic IList set -- is a private explicit implementation, so the settled BCL-interface rule already excludes them
System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC.listBinding: the view holds the list INSTANCE it was handed; an owner that later points its own field at a different list does not change an existing view, so a Go slice header is captured by value rather than by pointer
System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC.enumeration: forwarded to the underlying list, so the semantics are the LIST's and not the view's: an array-backed view is NOT version-checked, because SZArrayHelper.SZGenericArrayEnumerator<T> holds only _array, _index and _endIndex and an array cannot change length, while a List<T>-backed view keeps List<T>._version fail-fast
System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyC.elementEquality: EqualityComparer<T>.Default supplied per element type; for System.Single that is System.Single::Equals, which returns TRUE for two NaNs where Go's == returns false
